title: PRD: Language SDKs — composable pagination adapters, deterministic backoff, and streaming↔paged transition behavior
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Goal: Define a pragmatic, language-idiomatic SDK contract for Python/TypeScript/Go that makes pagination composable, retry/backoff deterministic across runtimes, and defines clear transition behavior when callers switch between streaming APIs and paged iteration.

Background: Teams building on Redwood need predictable semantics when paginating large result sets, retrying transient errors, and when converting long-running streaming responses into pageable results (and vice versa). Current SDK implementations diverge in subtle ways (cursor shape, retry windows, idempotency markers) which causes engineering friction and customer support churn.

Scope (in):
- Standardized adapter interfaces that let apps swap between offset-based fetch, cursor-based fetch, and streaming consumers without rewriting business logic.
- Canonical retry/backoff semantics (per-request idempotency hints, deterministic backoff algorithm, max-retry budget) documented and implemented in Python/TS/Go official SDKs.
- Explicit behavior when converting a streaming response to paged iteration (client-side buffering limits, resume tokens, partial-result guarantees).
- Compatibility rules and a deprecation policy for breaking shape or header changes.

Scope (out):
- End-to-end wire protocol changes on the server. (Server-side changes will be coordinated via separate runtime/eng issues.)
- Implementations for community SDKs (these are guidance-only).

Proposed contract highlights:
- Pagination adapter: an opaque "PageCursor" string plus an optional stable metadata map. SDKs expose a small adapter API: fetch_page(cursor?, page_size?) -> {items, next_cursor, partial, consumed_bytes}. Implementations must: preserve SDK-level opaque cursor, not expose internal IDs, and allow user-supplied transforms.
- Streaming->Paged transition: when a user requests streaming_to_page(max_buffer_tokens, max_items), the SDK must: (1) open a streaming connection, (2) buffer up to the configured limits, (3) surface pages with deterministic boundaries, (4) if the stream is truncated due to limits, surface a resume token usable with fetch_page.
- Retry semantics: default exponential backoff with jitter (base=200ms, factor=2, max_interval=5s), deterministic jitter seed derived from request id where available. Retries are gated by idempotency: read/list calls are retried by default; non-idempotent calls require explicit idempotency_key param.
- Compatibility: SDKs must implement a compatibility shim that detects server-side cursor format version and map legacy cursors to the current adapter where possible. Breaking cursor changes must be announced with a two-release deprecation window and automated migration helpers in each SDK.

Acceptance criteria (high level) are below. See attached links for reference PRD drafts and mock API surface examples.
comments: 2026-02-21: Triage meeting notes — PM + Eng + DX present. Action: refine streaming->paged memory limits and add a deterministic resume token format.

2026-02-27: Architecture sync — Eng team (Liam Chen, Priya Rao) proposed embedding a 12-byte versioning prefix in the PageCursor for forward/back-compat. Requires server support for cursor version header (ENG-9421 suggested dependency).
2026-03-03: Design review — Designer (Maya Feldman) requested example ergonomics for async iteration in Python and async generators in TS; small API tweaks accepted.

2026-03-08: Security review kickoff — Security asked for threat modelling around resume tokens leakage; added requirement to encrypt resume tokens at rest and mark them short-lived. Security review flag set true.
2026-03-12: Implementation plan approved by Eng lead. Split work across SDK teams: python (ENG-7182), ts (ENG-7183), go (ENG-7184). Backwards compatibility tests added to CI.
2026-03-12: PM follow-up — added acceptance criteria and rollout strategy notes.
acceptance_criteria: All three official SDKs (Python/TS/Go) implement the pagination adapter API with identical observable behavior for fetch_page and iterate_pages.
Streaming->paged transition implemented with configurable buffering; deterministic resume token produced when truncation occurs and validated in integration tests.
Retry/backoff logic implemented per spec (base=200ms, factor=2, max=5s) and deterministic jitter seeded by request id; unit tests cover deterministic jitter behavior.
Backward compatibility shim translates legacy cursors (v1) to current format (v2) in server+SDK integration tests; deprecation warnings emitted in SDK logs for legacy cursor usage.
Performance: page fetch median p95 latency delta vs current SDKs <= +10% for small pages (<=100 items) and throughput parity preserved under batching workloads.
Docs: PRD + API reference + migration guide published in Confluence and linked SDK README examples for Python/TS/Go.
Automated acceptance tests (integration) added to SDK CI and pass end-to-end against a staging runtime that includes cursor-version header support.
Rollout: feature gated behind server flag; SDKs default to conservative behavior and expose opt-in for new adapter, with telemetry to monitor errors and resume token failures.
Security: resume tokens are short-lived, encrypted-at-rest, and reviewed by Security; security sign-off recorded before general availability.
Release: SDK changes included in sdk-2026.04 release train with migration checklist and a 2-release deprecation window for legacy cursor behaviour.
notes: Engineering requested a small API sugar: page_iterator(chunk_size) that internally maps to fetch_page but appears idiomatic per language.
Design emphasized examples for both client-side resume and server-side-prefetch strategies; include both in README.
PM: prioritize deterministic retries and resume token security in first cut; adapter ergonomics can iterate post-MVP.
QA: add flaky-network scenarios and mis-ordered resume tokens test cases to CI matrix.
